The dated registration records the agreement, reference and prior base. Declared non-residents receive 20% withholding on taxable remuneration without resident personal, dependant or insurance deductions; that rule precedes the resident short-contract withholding rule and does not require a rate override. Resident progressive withholding uses the version’s monthly scale and deduction amounts; the configured year-end rule reconciles annual withholding. Before 1 July 2026, non-residents retain the earlier overtime-premium exemption and taxable leave cash-out. The full qualifying overtime and statutory cessation leave exemptions apply to residents from tax year 2026 and non-residents from 1 July 2026 (Decree 253/2026 arts.26 and 69). A future departure does not establish cessation in the current period. Payments beyond statutory limits remain taxable. Special tax profiles require further verification. Tax residence is a fact the employer records: a resident is present 183 days in the calendar year or twelve months from arrival, or has a registered permanent residence or a rented home for 183 days or more (Decree 253/2026 art.4), and anyone else is non-resident (art.5); neither the Law nor the decree presumes either for an unknown residence, so an unrecorded residence stops the calculation (`terms.tax_residency`). Residence governs the whole tax period (art.66(1)(a): the calendar year, or the first twelve months from arrival): each month is withheld on the status recorded for it (art.46(3), art.64(4): income is taxed when paid), and a change of status during the year is settled in the annual finalisation, which re-prices the year’s wage income on the resident table and credits what was withheld at 20% (art.51; Decree 126/2020 art.8(6)(d)); earlier months are never re-withheld. Leave cash-out: art.26(2) exempts the pay for untaken leave only within the Labour Code art.113(3) conditions and rate (the Decree 145/2020 art.67(3) day), and art.26(3) taxes the excess; income is taxed in the month it is paid (art.46(3)), so an excess is income of the paying month and is never spread over earlier periods. Meal: Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(g.5) — a cash mid-shift meal is taxable only above the Labour Ministry cap of 730,000 a month (Circular 26/2016/TT-BLĐTBXH); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(g) keeps 730,000 until art.69(1)(b) lifts it to 1,200,000 from 1 July 2026. A class counting toward PIT.MEAL enters the base only above that cap. Housing: rent, power and water the employer pays on the worker’s behalf is taxable at the amount paid but not above 15% of the worker’s other taxable income at the unit (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(đ)(đ.1); Decree 253/2026 art.8(2)(h)); a class counting toward PIT.HOUSING enters at the lower of the two. Decree 253/2026 arts.69(1)(a),70(2) apply the resident wage rules to tax year 2026 while preserving pre-July filings under the former rules for adjustment at annual finalisation. Dependants are the PIT election dependants — the dependants registered with the tax authority (scheme.elections.dependants). Non-residents: 20% of taxable income, no deductions. Insurance deducted is the employee's compulsory SI, HI and UI actually charged in the month (charged.month), exact in a bonus month (Law 109/2025/QH15 art.8(2); Law 04/2007 art.15 before 2026). Engine (round 7): the meal allowance is taxable only above 730,000 a month (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(g.5)); housing the employer pays is taxable up to 15% of the other taxable income (Circular 111/2013 art.2(2)(đ)); employer pension/life-insurance contributions are taxable and, with the employee's own, deducted up to 1,000,000 a month (Circular 111/2013 art.9(2)(c)). A resident with no labour contract (employment_type SERVICE) or one under three months is withheld 10% on a payment of 2,000,000 or more (Circular 111/2013 art.25(1)(i)), nothing below it or with the commitment form. December finalises the year for an employee who authorised it (PIT election finalisation_authorised): the annual table (Law 109/2025 art.9) on the year's assessed income less the year's insurance and twelve months' deductions, less the tax already withheld (Decree 253/2026 art.51). Quyết định 61/QĐ-TLĐ of the Vietnam General Confederation of Labour, in force from 1 July 2025, cut the dues of a member in an enterprise outside the State sector to 0.5% of the salary the compulsory social insurance is based on, capped at 10% of the base salary (mức lương cơ sở) — the 1% of Decision 1908/QĐ-TLĐ no longer stands on any version here. https://pbgdpl.cantho.gov.vn/quyet-dinh-61qd-tld-ve-dieu-chinh-giam-muc-dong-doan-phi-cong-doan https://nhandan.vn/chinh-thuc-giam-muc-dong-doan-phi-cong-doan-tu-172025-post898504.html [DEC61] art.1 (city-portal transcription) waives dues only for a member on SI benefit for a month or more, or without work, income or pay for a month or more — not for the 14 unpaid working days that end the month’s SI contribution (Law 41/2024 art.33(5)); such a member still pays 0.5% of the insurance salary (the contractual salary and fixed supplements within the reference-level floor and ceiling).
